runs.t: ACID describes atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability of database transactions. It provides a framework for reasoning about reliable state changes, but exact isolation guarantees vary by database and configuration.

Atomicity means all-or-nothing; consistency preserves declared constraints when transactions are correct; isolation addresses interfering operations; durability retains committed results after specified failures. Use constraints and transactions together.
An order transaction creates a payment record and deducts store credit in one commit. If the write fails, neither partial operation should become visible as successful.
ACID does not guarantee that your business logic is correct or that external email/card APIs participate atomically. A database may use weaker default isolation than you assume.
